title: Recording and teaching in Paris; the Dizzy Gillespie label tapes
summary: After the tour he recorded with John Lewis and Cecil Payne for the DG label, poorly distributed by Dave Usher.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So well now, we haven't got all the time in the world, so I've got to get you from that festival --
-- you came -- you know, one of the things is I've got a note here that says after the end of the tour with Dizzy that you did some recording and teaching in Paris. Did you?
Oh, yes, I did. Yes, I did.
You got a taste for that, too.
We did quite a few things with John, with Cecil Payne, and we put the -- I took those tapes home and we put those tapes out on the DG label, the Dizzy Gillespie label.
Uh-huh. Which they weren't exploited to the nth degree, you know.
No, no, because there was a friend of Dizzy's named Dave Usher, from Detroit, who was taking care of the distribution, which he didn't know very well.
The record business was new to him, you know.
